vs-code.tagline: Lightweight, extensible editor from Microsoft, the market standard.
vs-code.description: Free code editor with a built-in debugger, terminal and Git. A huge extension ecosystem covers practically any language and workflow.

cursor.tagline: VS Code fork with AI built into the editing flow.
cursor.description: Editor based on VS Code with chat, multi-file editing and AI agents inside the editor. Keeps VS Code extensions and shortcuts.

neovim.tagline: Modern Vim, configurable in Lua, 100% keyboard.
neovim.description: Vim fork with a rebuilt architecture, built-in LSP support and Lua configuration. Runs in the terminal and has a vast plugin ecosystem.

jetbrains-ides.tagline: IntelliJ, WebStorm, PyCharm: deep refactoring and analysis.
jetbrains-ides.description: A family of per-language IDEs with advanced refactoring, code inspections and debugging. There are free (Community) and paid editions.

zed.tagline: Very fast editor written in Rust, with collaborative editing.
zed.description: High-performance code editor written in Rust, with real-time collaboration and built-in AI features.

sublime-text.tagline: Fast editor, great for huge files.
sublime-text.description: Light, fast editor with multiple selections and powerful search. Paid license with an unlimited evaluation period.

helix.tagline: Post-Vim modal editor with built-in LSP and tree-sitter.
helix.description: Modal terminal editor where selection comes before action. LSP, tree-sitter and multiple cursors work without plugins.

xcode.tagline: Apple's official IDE for iOS and macOS.
xcode.description: Apple's IDE for building iOS, macOS, watchOS and visionOS apps, with simulators, Interface Builder and Instruments. Runs on macOS only.

git.tagline: Distributed version control, the foundation of it all.
git.description: Distributed version control system created by Linus Torvalds. It underpins GitHub, GitLab and most modern development.

github.tagline: Repository hosting, PRs, Actions and Copilot.
github.description: Code hosting platform with pull requests, issues, CI/CD (Actions) and the Copilot assistant. The largest open source community in the world.

gitlab.tagline: Complete DevOps platform, can be self-hosted.
gitlab.description: Platform that brings together repositories, CI/CD, security and project management. Can be used in the cloud or installed on your own server.

bitbucket.description: Atlassian's Git repository hosting, with Pipelines for CI/CD and direct integration with Jira and Confluence.

lazygit.tagline: Terminal UI for Git that saves you commands.
lazygit.description: Terminal interface (TUI) for Git: staging by hunk, interactive rebase and conflict resolution with a few keystrokes.

github-cli.tagline: Create PRs and issues straight from the terminal with gh.
github-cli.description: GitHub's official command-line client (the gh command): opens and reviews pull requests, manages issues and releases, and calls the API.

gitea.description: Self-hosted Git service written in Go, light enough to run on a small server. Includes issues, PRs and CI (Actions).

pre-commit.tagline: Multi-language Git hooks, managed through config.
pre-commit.description: Framework that manages Git hooks from a configuration file, running linters and formatters before every commit.

react.description: Library for building interfaces out of declarative components. It is the foundation of frameworks like Next.js and of much of the modern web.

nextjs.tagline: React framework with SSR, routing and edge.
nextjs.description: Full-stack framework on top of React, with file-based routing, server rendering, static generation and ready-made optimizations.

vite.description: Build tool with a very fast development server (native ES modules) and production bundling through Rollup.

tailwindcss.description: CSS framework built on utility classes: you style directly in the HTML using design tokens, without hand-writing CSS.

svelte.tagline: UI compiler with no virtual DOM.
svelte.description: Framework that compiles components into lean JavaScript at build time, with no virtual DOM. Reactivity through runes and a simple syntax.

astro.tagline: Content sites with zero JS by default.
astro.description: Framework for content-driven sites that ships little or no JavaScript to the browser. Accepts React, Svelte and other components.

shadcn-ui.tagline: Copyable components built on Radix and Tailwind.
shadcn-ui.description: Collection of accessible components that you copy into your project instead of installing as a dependency, with Radix and Tailwind underneath.

threejs.description: JavaScript library for 3D scenes in the browser on top of WebGL and WebGPU. The basis of projects like React Three Fiber.

nodejs.description: JavaScript runtime built on the V8 engine, used for servers, build tools and scripts. Ships with the npm package manager.

bun.tagline: All-in-one runtime, bundler and package manager.
bun.description: JavaScript and TypeScript runtime with a built-in bundler, test runner and package manager, focused on speed.

fastapi.tagline: Fast, typed Python APIs with automatic docs.
fastapi.description: Python framework for APIs that uses type hints to validate data and generate OpenAPI documentation automatically. Supports async.

django.tagline: Full-featured Python framework with ORM and admin.
django.description: "Batteries included" Python framework: ORM, authentication, admin panel and migrations come ready to use.

express.description: Minimal, flexible web framework for Node.js, with routing and middleware. One of the most widely used in the ecosystem.

hono.tagline: Ultralight web framework for edge and Node.
hono.description: Small, fast web framework built on Web standards, running on Cloudflare Workers, Bun, Deno and Node.

trpc.description: Lets you call server functions from the client with shared TypeScript types, without generating a schema or code.

graphql.description: Query language and specification for APIs where the client asks for exactly the fields it needs. Here, the JavaScript reference implementation.

postgresql.description: Open source relational database known for SQL compliance, reliable transactions and extensions such as PostGIS and pgvector.

supabase.description: Open backend platform built on Postgres, with authentication, file storage, functions and realtime.

sqlite.tagline: Embedded database in a single file.
sqlite.description: Embedded SQL engine with no server that keeps everything in a single file. It is in browsers, phones and countless applications.

redis.description: In-memory data structure store, used as a cache, queue and key-value database. Optional persistence to disk.

mongodb.description: NoSQL database oriented to JSON documents (BSON), with a flexible schema. Available self-hosted or as a service (Atlas).

prisma.tagline: TypeScript ORM with a declarative schema.
prisma.description: ORM for Node.js and TypeScript with a declarative schema, migrations and a fully typed client.

drizzle-orm.tagline: Lightweight TypeScript ORM, close to SQL.
drizzle-orm.description: Thin TypeScript ORM, with the schema written in code and queries that mirror SQL. No client generation step.

dbeaver.description: Graphical client that connects to dozens of databases via JDBC, with a SQL editor, data browser and ER diagrams. Free Community edition.

docker.tagline: Containers to package and run any app.
docker.description: Platform for packaging applications and their dependencies into portable containers. Docker Desktop is paid for large companies.

kubernetes.description: Open source system to deploy, scale and manage containerized applications across clusters of machines.

vercel.tagline: Deploy frontends and functions with previews.
vercel.description: Hosting platform for frontends and serverless functions, with a deploy on every push and preview URLs. Creator of Next.js.

cloudflare.tagline: CDN, Workers, DNS and edge security.
cloudflare.description: Global network with CDN, DNS, attack protection and an edge compute platform (Workers, Pages, R2, D1).

terraform.description: HashiCorp tool for describing infrastructure in declarative files and applying it across several cloud providers. BUSL license since 2023.

github-actions.description: Build, test and deploy automation defined in YAML files in the repository itself. Free for public repositories.

aws.tagline: The largest catalog of cloud services.
aws.description: Amazon Web Services: hundreds of compute, storage, database and networking services, billed by usage, with a limited free tier.

grafana.description: Dashboard and alerting platform that queries Prometheus, Loki and dozens of other sources. Can be self-hosted or used on Grafana Cloud.

vitest.description: Testing framework that reuses the Vite configuration, with a Jest-compatible API, TypeScript and a fast watch mode.

jest.description: Testing framework with mocks, snapshots and coverage built in. Widely used in React and Node projects.

playwright.description: Browser automation for E2E tests on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with auto-waiting, traces and test recording.

cypress.tagline: E2E with an interactive debugging UI.
cypress.description: E2E testing tool that runs in the browser, with an interactive interface to watch and debug each step of the test.

eslint.description: Static analyzer that finds errors and inconsistencies in JavaScript and TypeScript, with configurable rules and plugins.

prettier.description: Code formatter with few options that rewrites the file in a single style. Supports JS, TS, CSS, Markdown and more.

biome.tagline: Very fast linter and formatter in Rust.
biome.description: Single lint and formatting tool, written in Rust, that replaces ESLint and Prettier in many projects with a big speed gain.

sonarqube.tagline: Static analysis for quality and security.
sonarqube.description: Platform that analyzes code for bugs, vulnerabilities and technical debt. Free Community edition; additional paid editions.

claude-code.tagline: Coding agent in the terminal and the IDE.
claude-code.description: Anthropic's programming agent that reads the project, edits files and runs commands from the terminal, with IDE extensions.

github-copilot.tagline: Code autocomplete and chat in the editor.
github-copilot.description: GitHub/Microsoft coding assistant with inline suggestions, chat and agent mode inside VS Code, JetBrains and other editors.

postman.description: Platform to design, test and document APIs, with shareable collections and test automation.

insomnia.description: API client for REST, GraphQL and gRPC, with a lean interface, environment variables and local storage.

raycast.tagline: Launcher with commands, snippets and extensions.
raycast.description: Command launcher for macOS with search, snippets, a window manager and a store of community-made extensions.

warp.tagline: Modern terminal with blocks and AI.
warp.description: Terminal that groups each command's output into blocks and brings AI assistance, better history and modern text editing.

figma.description: Browser-based interface design tool, with real-time collaboration and a dev mode to inspect measurements and code.

obsidian.tagline: Markdown notes with links between ideas.
obsidian.description: Notes app that stores everything in local Markdown files, with links between notes, a connection graph and plugins. Free for personal use.

visual-studio.tagline: Microsoft's full IDE for .NET and C++ on Windows.
visual-studio.description: Microsoft IDE with a debugger, profiler and tools for .NET, C++ and game development. The Community edition is free for individuals and small teams.

android-studio.tagline: Google's official IDE for Android apps.
android-studio.description: Free IntelliJ-based IDE with emulators, a layout editor and performance profiling tools for Android.

eclipse.tagline: Classic open source IDE for Java, extensible through plugins.
eclipse.description: Free, modular IDE widely used in Java and in enterprise environments, with a large plugin collection.

netbeans.tagline: Free Apache IDE for Java and other languages.
netbeans.description: Open source IDE maintained by Apache, with support for Java, PHP, JavaScript and built-in Maven.

emacs.tagline: Lisp-extensible editor that becomes almost an operating system.
emacs.description: Text editor programmable in Emacs Lisp, with a huge package ecosystem (Org mode, Magit, LSP) and over four decades of history.

vim.tagline: The classic modal editor, present on almost every server.
vim.description: Highly configurable modal text editor, installed by default on many Unix systems. The base of the whole Vim family.

nano.tagline: Simple terminal editor with no learning curve.
nano.description: Small, easy terminal text editor with the shortcuts listed on screen. Comes preinstalled on many Linux distributions.

kakoune.tagline: Modal editor where selection comes before action.
kakoune.description: Terminal modal editor with a selection-first philosophy, native multiple cursors and integration with external tools through the shell.

micro.tagline: Modern terminal editor with common shortcuts (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+C).
micro.description: Terminal editor written in Go, single binary, with familiar shortcuts, mouse support, multiple cursors and plugin support.

lapce.tagline: Native Rust editor, lightweight with built-in LSP.
lapce.description: Open source code editor written in Rust, with GPU rendering, optional modal editing and WASI plugin support.

vscodium.tagline: VS Code built without Microsoft's telemetry and branding.
vscodium.description: Community distribution of VS Code built from the open source code, with no telemetry or proprietary Microsoft binaries.

notepad-plus-plus.tagline: Lightweight Windows editor with tabs and syntax highlighting.
notepad-plus-plus.description: Free, light text editor for Windows, with tabs, macros, advanced search and support for dozens of languages.

doom-emacs.tagline: Ready-made Emacs configuration with Vim-style keybindings.
doom-emacs.description: Emacs configuration framework focused on speed, with Evil (Vim-style) mode by default, ready to use in minutes.

lazyvim.tagline: Ready-made Neovim distribution, configurable in Lua.
lazyvim.description: Complete Neovim setup on top of the lazy.nvim plugin manager, with LSP, search, Git and a theme already integrated and easy to extend.

alacritty.description: Terminal emulator focused on performance and simplicity, configured by file, with no tabs or splits (use it with tmux).

kitty.tagline: Fast GPU terminal with tabs, splits and images.
kitty.description: Terminal emulator with GPU rendering, tabs, splits, a graphics protocol for images and Python scripting.

wezterm.description: GPU terminal emulator with a built-in multiplexer (tabs, panes, remote sessions) and programmable Lua configuration.

ghostty.tagline: Fast, native terminal with a platform-specific UI.
ghostty.description: Terminal emulator with GPU rendering and a native interface on macOS and Linux, balancing features and performance.

tmux.tagline: Terminal multiplexer: persistent sessions, windows and panes.
tmux.description: Lets you split the terminal into panes, keep sessions alive after disconnecting and resume them later, widely used on servers over SSH.

zellij.tagline: Modern terminal multiplexer with on-screen hints.
zellij.description: Rust multiplexer with layouts, floating panes, WebAssembly plugins and a help bar that shows the shortcuts.

windows-terminal.tagline: Microsoft's modern terminal with tabs for PowerShell, CMD and WSL.
windows-terminal.description: Free Windows terminal with tabs, panes, GPU rendering and profiles for PowerShell, CMD and WSL distributions.

iterm2.tagline: Powerful macOS terminal with splits and search.
iterm2.description: Replacement for macOS Terminal with splits, profiles, search, paste history and shell integration.

fish.tagline: Shell with autosuggestions and colors out of the box.
fish.description: Interactive shell with autosuggestions, syntax highlighting and completions built in, comfortable without needing plugins.

starship.tagline: Fast terminal prompt that works with any shell.
starship.description: Fast, configurable Rust prompt that shows the Git branch, language versions and command status in bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell and others.

oh-my-zsh.tagline: Zsh configuration framework with plugins and themes.
oh-my-zsh.description: Zsh configuration manager with hundreds of plugins and themes, popular for getting a productive shell in minutes.

nushell.tagline: Shell that treats command output as data tables.
nushell.description: Modern Rust shell where commands return structured data (tables, JSON), making it easy to filter and transform results.

code-server.tagline: VS Code in the browser, hosted on your own machine.
code-server.description: Runs VS Code on a server and exposes it in the browser, letting you code from any device with an environment and machine you control.

github-codespaces.tagline: Cloud development environments, straight from the repository.
github-codespaces.description: Development environments hosted by GitHub, opened in the browser or in VS Code, configured through devcontainer and ready in seconds.

stackblitz.tagline: Node.js environment that runs inside the browser (WebContainers).
stackblitz.description: Online editor that runs Node.js in the browser itself, useful for prototypes, examples and bug reproductions shareable by link.

git-lfs.tagline: Keeps large files out of the Git repository.
git-lfs.description: Git extension that replaces large files (images, videos, models) with lightweight pointers and stores them on a separate server.

gitkraken.tagline: Graphical Git client with a clear view of history.
gitkraken.description: Desktop Git client with a commit graph, visual conflict resolution and integration with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket.

sourcetree.tagline: Free graphical Git client from Atlassian.
sourcetree.description: Free Git client for Windows and macOS, with branch visualization, hunk staging and Bitbucket integration.

github-desktop.tagline: Simple Git client built for the GitHub workflow.
github-desktop.description: Free, simple app to clone, commit and open pull requests on GitHub without using the command line.

tig.description: Ncurses interface to explore history, diffs, blame and the file tree of a Git repository right in the terminal.

gitui.tagline: Fast Git terminal interface written in Rust.
gitui.description: Git TUI with staging, commits, branches, stash and log, designed to be fast even on large repositories.

delta.description: Pager for git diff, log and blame with syntax highlighting, line numbers and word-level differences.

difftastic.tagline: Diff that understands the code's syntax structure.
difftastic.description: Diff tool that compares the syntax tree instead of lines, ignoring formatting changes and showing what actually changed.

husky.tagline: Simple Git hooks for Node projects.
husky.description: Sets up Git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg) through package.json, running lint and tests before each commit.

lefthook.tagline: Fast Git hook manager in a single binary.
lefthook.description: Hook manager written in Go with parallel execution and YAML configuration, independent of the project's language.

lint-staged.tagline: Runs linters only on the files in the commit.
lint-staged.description: Runs linters and formatters only on staged files, keeping the pre-commit hook fast even in large projects.

commitlint.tagline: Checks whether commit messages follow a convention.
commitlint.description: Validates commit messages against configurable rules, such as Conventional Commits, usually in a commit-msg hook.

commitizen.tagline: Interactive assistant for writing conventional commits.
commitizen.description: CLI that guides commit message writing through prompts, producing consistent messages in the Conventional Commits format.

semantic-release.tagline: Automates versioning, changelog and publishing from commits.
semantic-release.description: Decides the next semantic version from commit messages, generates the changelog and publishes the package automatically in CI.

changesets.tagline: Versioning and changelogs for monorepos, with change files.
changesets.description: Each PR brings a file describing the change; the tool calculates versions and generates changelogs, with good monorepo support.

release-please.tagline: Keeps a release PR up to date from commits.
release-please.description: Maintained by Google, it opens and updates a release pull request with the version and changelog calculated from commits; on merge, it creates the release.

git-cliff.tagline: Customizable changelog generator from Git history.
git-cliff.description: Generates changelogs from history and Conventional Commits, with fully configurable templates, in a single binary.

jujutsu.tagline: Git-compatible version control with a simpler model.
jujutsu.description: VCS that uses Git repositories as storage but with a different working model: no staging, easily rewritten history and first-class conflicts.

mercurial.tagline: Distributed version control system, an alternative to Git.
mercurial.description: Distributed VCS known for consistent commands and good scalability, used in large codebases.

forgejo.description: Lightweight, self-hostable Git platform derived from Gitea and governed by a nonprofit organization, with issues, PRs and Actions.

codeberg.tagline: Free, nonprofit Git hosting for open source.
codeberg.description: Code hosting platform run by a nonprofit association, based on Forgejo, aimed at free software projects.

azure-devops.tagline: Microsoft's repositories, pipelines and work management.
azure-devops.description: Microsoft suite with Git repositories, CI/CD pipelines, work boards and test management, widely used in enterprises.

gh-dash.tagline: GitHub PR and issue dashboard in the terminal.
gh-dash.description: GitHub CLI extension that shows pull requests and issues in sections configurable by filters, right in the terminal.

renovate.tagline: Updates dependencies automatically via pull requests.
renovate.description: Bot that detects outdated dependencies across dozens of package managers and opens update PRs, with configurable grouping and scheduling.

dependabot.tagline: GitHub's native dependency updates and alerts.
dependabot.description: GitHub feature that alerts about vulnerable dependencies and opens update pull requests, enabled by a configuration file.

gitleaks.tagline: Detects leaked secrets in code and Git history.
gitleaks.description: Scans repositories and commits for API keys, passwords and tokens, and can run in hooks and in CI.

trufflehog.tagline: Finds and verifies leaked secrets in repositories and other sources.
trufflehog.description: Searches repositories, buckets and other sources for credentials and tries to verify whether they are still active, reducing false positives.

sourcehut.tagline: Minimalist, fast software forge with no required JavaScript.
sourcehut.description: Hosting platform with Git and Mercurial repositories, mailing lists for patches and CI, with a light interface and paid by subscription.

gerrit.tagline: Rigorous code review on top of Git, used in large projects.
gerrit.description: Code review server for Git where each change is reviewed and approved individually before landing, used by projects such as Android.

vue.tagline: Progressive UI framework, easy to adopt gradually.
vue.description: JavaScript framework for interfaces with single-file components and simple reactivity, which can be adopted gradually on a page or used for full apps.

nuxt.tagline: Full-stack framework on top of Vue, with SSR and file-based routes.
nuxt.description: Framework for Vue applications with file-based routing, server rendering, static generation and ready-made modules.

angular.tagline: Google's complete framework, with TypeScript and dependency injection.
angular.description: Complete platform for web applications, with routing, forms, HTTP, testing and CLI built in, based on TypeScript.

solidjs.tagline: Fine-grained reactive UI, with React-like syntax.
solidjs.description: UI library with signal-based reactivity and no virtual DOM, with JSX similar to React's and very high performance.

preact.tagline: 3 KB alternative to React, almost fully compatible.
preact.description: Tiny UI library with the same modern API as React and a compatibility layer to use libraries from the React ecosystem.

qwik.tagline: Framework that loads JavaScript only when the user interacts.
qwik.description: Framework with resumability: the server sends already-interactive HTML and JavaScript is downloaded on demand, reducing load time.

react-router.tagline: Routing and full-stack framework for React (Remix's successor).
react-router.description: React routing library that, from v7, also works as a framework with data loading, SSR and actions, incorporating Remix.

sveltekit.description: Application framework for Svelte with file-based routing, SSR, static generation and adapters for several hosting providers.

htmx.tagline: Interactivity through HTML attributes, with no JavaScript to write.
htmx.description: Library that lets you make requests, swap page fragments and use WebSockets with just HTML attributes, keeping logic on the server.

alpinejs.tagline: Lightweight reactivity, declared straight in the HTML.
alpinejs.description: Tiny framework that adds reactivity and behavior to HTML with attributes, in the style of Vue and Tailwind, with no build step.

lit.tagline: Library for building fast, light Web Components.
lit.description: Small Google library for creating standard Web Components that work in any framework or none at all.

typescript.description: JavaScript superset that adds static typing, catching errors before execution and improving autocomplete in editors.

webpack.tagline: Established, configurable bundler with a huge ecosystem.
webpack.description: Highly configurable module bundler, with loaders and plugins for practically any file type.

esbuild.tagline: Extremely fast bundler and minifier, written in Go.
esbuild.description: JavaScript and TypeScript bundler and minifier written in Go, tens of times faster than traditional alternatives.

rollup.tagline: Bundler focused on ES modules, ideal for libraries.
rollup.description: ES module bundler with efficient tree-shaking, widely used to publish libraries and as the basis of Vite's build.

parcel.tagline: Zero-config bundler: point it at the HTML and go.
parcel.description: Bundler that detects what the project uses and configures itself, with a dev server, hot reload and production optimizations.

redux-toolkit.tagline: The official, modern way to use Redux.
redux-toolkit.description: Official toolset for Redux that cuts boilerplate and includes RTK Query for fetching and caching data.

zustand.tagline: Minimal global state for React, with no boilerplate.
zustand.description: Small hook-based state library for React, with a minimal API and no need for providers.

tanstack-query.tagline: Server data fetching, caching and synchronization.
tanstack-query.description: Manages server data with caching, background revalidation, pagination and ready-made loading and error states.

radix-ui.tagline: Accessible, unstyled UI primitives for React.
radix-ui.description: Unstyled components (dialogs, menus, tabs) with accessibility and focus handled correctly, for you to style as you wish.

mui.tagline: React component library based on Material Design.
mui.description: Large set of ready-made React components following Material Design, with customizable theming and paid versions with advanced components.

chakra-ui.tagline: Accessible React components, with style props.
chakra-ui.description: React component library focused on accessibility and productivity, using style props and a theming system.

bootstrap.tagline: Classic CSS framework, with grid and ready-made components.
bootstrap.description: CSS and JavaScript framework with a responsive grid and dozens of ready-made components, widely used in sites and dashboards.

motion.tagline: Animation library for React and JavaScript (formerly Framer Motion).
motion.description: Declarative animation library with gestures, layout and exit transitions, with a React version and a plain JavaScript one.

storybook.tagline: Workshop to develop, document and test UI components.
storybook.description: Isolated environment to build components, document their variations and test them visually, compatible with the main frameworks.

react-three-fiber.tagline: Three.js the declarative way, with React components.
react-three-fiber.description: React renderer for Three.js that lets you build 3D scenes with components and hooks, with a large ecosystem of helpers (drei).

d3.tagline: Custom data visualizations in SVG and Canvas.
d3.description: Low-level library for binding data to the DOM and creating fully custom visualizations, with scales, shapes and layouts.

chartjs.description: Library with the most common chart types (bar, line, pie, radar), responsive and with animations built in.

react-hook-form.description: Hook-based form library with few re-renders and integration with validators such as Zod.

pnpm.tagline: Fast package manager that saves disk space.
pnpm.description: Package manager for Node.js that stores each version once on disk and links it into projects, with great monorepo support.

deno.tagline: Secure runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript, with native TypeScript.
deno.description: Runtime created by Node.js's author, with zero-config TypeScript, explicit permissions, a standard library and built-in tooling.

flask.description: Python web microframework with a small core and optional extensions, letting you choose the project's pieces.

nestjs.tagline: Node framework with modular architecture, inspired by Angular.
nestjs.description: Framework for Node.js and TypeScript backends with modules, dependency injection and decorators, running on top of Express or Fastify.

fastify.tagline: Node HTTP framework focused on performance and validation.
fastify.description: Web framework for Node.js with low overhead, JSON Schema validation, a plugin system and built-in logging.

laravel.description: PHP framework with an ORM (Eloquent), queues, authentication, migrations and a broad ecosystem, known for a good developer experience.

rails.tagline: Ruby framework built on convention over configuration.
rails.description: Complete Ruby web framework with ORM, routes, jobs and generators, which popularized the idea of convention over configuration.

spring-boot.tagline: The enterprise standard for Java and Kotlin services.
spring-boot.description: Framework that simplifies building production-ready Spring applications, with auto-configuration, an embedded server and metrics.

aspnet-core.tagline: Microsoft's cross-platform, fast web framework for C#.
aspnet-core.description: Framework for APIs and web applications in C# and .NET, cross-platform, high-performance and tightly integrated with the Microsoft ecosystem.

gin.tagline: Fast, popular HTTP framework for Go.
gin.description: Go web framework with a high-performance router, middleware and data validation, widely used for REST APIs.

axum.tagline: Ergonomic Rust web framework, built on Tokio and Tower.
axum.description: Modular, asynchronous Rust web framework built on Tokio, Hyper and Tower, with typed extractors for requests.

phoenix.tagline: Elixir framework for real-time, highly concurrent apps.
phoenix.description: Elixir web framework with channels, LiveView for real-time interfaces and the robustness of the Erlang virtual machine.

go.tagline: Simple compiled language, great for services and tools.
go.description: Google language with fast compilation, built-in concurrency (goroutines) and single binaries, widely used in infrastructure and APIs.

rust.tagline: Systems language with memory safety and high performance.
rust.description: Compiled language that guarantees memory safety without a garbage collector, with performance close to C and C++.

python.tagline: Versatile language, a leader in data, AI and automation.
python.description: Language with clear syntax used in web, automation, data science and AI, with a broad standard library and a giant ecosystem.

authjs.tagline: Authentication for web apps with dozens of ready-made providers.
authjs.description: Authentication library (formerly NextAuth) with social login, email and credentials, sessions and database adapters for several frameworks.

keycloak.tagline: Open source identity server with SSO and OAuth/OIDC.
keycloak.description: Identity and access management platform with single sign-on, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML and user administration, self-hostable.

openapi-generator.tagline: Generates clients and servers from an OpenAPI specification.
openapi-generator.description: Generates client SDKs, server stubs and documentation in dozens of languages from an OpenAPI file.

grpc.tagline: High-performance RPC with Protocol Buffers contracts.
grpc.description: Google's remote procedure call framework, with Protobuf contracts, bidirectional streaming and code generation for several languages.

rabbitmq.tagline: Mature message broker, with queues and flexible routing.
rabbitmq.description: Message broker implementing AMQP, with queues, exchanges and acknowledgements, used to decouple services and distribute work.

kafka.description: Distributed platform to publish, store and process event streams at scale, with retention and replay.

bullmq.tagline: Job queues for Node.js on top of Redis.
bullmq.description: Redis-based queue library for Node.js, with delayed jobs, retries, priorities, rate limits and parallel processing.

zod.tagline: Data validation with schemas and inferred TypeScript types.
zod.description: Schema library for TypeScript that validates data at runtime and infers static types from the same schema.

pydantic.tagline: Data validation in Python using type hints.
pydantic.description: Library that validates and converts data in Python from type annotations, the basis of FastAPI and many AI tools.

socket-io.tagline: Bidirectional real-time communication, with automatic reconnection.
socket-io.description: Library for real-time communication between client and server, over WebSocket with fallback, rooms, reconnection and acknowledgements.

temporal.tagline: Durable workflows: code that survives failures and restarts.
temporal.description: Durable execution platform that resumes long workflows exactly where they stopped, with managed retries, timers and state.

strapi.tagline: Headless CMS on Node, with a ready-made panel and API.
strapi.description: Open source headless CMS where you model content in the panel and get a ready-made REST or GraphQL API.

pocketbase.tagline: Complete backend in a single file, with SQLite, auth and admin panel.
pocketbase.description: Open source backend in a single Go executable, with a SQLite database, authentication, file storage, realtime and an admin dashboard.

swagger-ui.description: Generates an interactive documentation page from an OpenAPI specification, where you can test endpoints in the browser itself.

apollo-server.tagline: GraphQL server for Node.js, popular and extensible.
apollo-server.description: GraphQL server for Node.js that works with several HTTP frameworks, with caching, plugins and good developer tooling.

elysia.tagline: Framework for Bun with end-to-end types.
elysia.description: Web framework designed for Bun, with built-in validation and end-to-end type inference between server and client.

mysql.tagline: Popular relational database, the base of much of the web.
mysql.description: Oracle's open source relational database, widely used in web applications and the LAMP stack, with replication and good documentation.

mariadb.tagline: Community fork of MySQL, compatible and fully open source.
mariadb.description: Relational database created by MySQL's original authors, with broad compatibility, extra storage engines and open governance.

clickhouse.tagline: Ultra-fast columnar database for large-scale analytics.
clickhouse.description: Columnar database for analytical (OLAP) queries over billions of rows in real time, used for metrics, logs and events.

duckdb.tagline: SQLite for analytics: a fast embedded analytical database.
duckdb.description: Embedded analytical database that runs in-process and queries CSV, Parquet and JSON files directly with SQL.

opensearch.tagline: Distributed search and analytics, forked from Elasticsearch.
opensearch.description: Distributed search and analytics engine, Apache-licensed, used for full-text search, logs and observability.

meilisearch.tagline: Fast, typo-tolerant search that is easy to use.
meilisearch.description: Open source search engine with instant results, typo tolerance and minimal configuration.

typesense.tagline: Fast in-memory search engine with vector search.
typesense.description: Open source C++ search engine that keeps the index in memory, with typo tolerance, facets and vector search.

neo4j.tagline: Graph database with the Cypher query language.
neo4j.description: Graph database that stores nodes and relationships as first-class citizens, ideal for highly connected data.

cassandra.tagline: Distributed database with high availability and write scale.
cassandra.description: Wide-column NoSQL database with no single point of failure, designed for very high write volume and geographic distribution.

dynamodb.tagline: AWS's serverless NoSQL database, with steady latency at any scale.
dynamodb.description: Fully managed key-value and document database, with automatic scaling and pay-per-use billing, integrated with the rest of AWS.

firebase.tagline: Google's backend platform for web and mobile apps.
firebase.description: Set of managed Google services with a realtime database (Firestore), authentication, hosting, functions and notifications.

neon.description: Managed Postgres with separated storage and compute, scale-to-zero and instant database branches for development and testing.

turso.tagline: Distributed SQLite at the edge, based on libSQL.
turso.description: Database based on libSQL (a SQLite fork) with replicas close to users, good for edge apps and a database per user.

minio.description: High-performance object storage server with an Amazon S3-compatible API, to run on your own infrastructure.

qdrant.tagline: Rust vector database for similarity search.
qdrant.description: Vector database for similarity search over embeddings, with metadata filtering, used in RAG and recommendations.

pgvector.description: PostgreSQL extension that stores embeddings and does similarity search with indexes, alongside your other relational data.

chroma.tagline: Simple embeddings database, built for AI apps.
chroma.description: Open source vector database with a simple Python and JavaScript API, designed for prototyping and building LLM applications.

kysely.tagline: SQL query builder with strong TypeScript types.
kysely.description: Typed query builder for TypeScript that checks queries against your schema without hiding the SQL underneath.

typeorm.tagline: ORM with decorators for TypeScript and JavaScript.
typeorm.description: ORM that maps classes and decorators to tables, with support for several databases, migrations and the Active Record and Data Mapper patterns.

sqlalchemy.tagline: Python's standard ORM and SQL toolkit.
sqlalchemy.description: Library with a powerful ORM and a low-level SQL layer, very flexible, the basis of many Python projects outside Django.

flyway.tagline: Versioned database migrations in plain SQL.
flyway.description: Migration tool that applies versioned SQL scripts in the right order, tracking database state, with a free community edition.

alembic.description: Migration tool from SQLAlchemy's author that generates and applies versioned migrations and can detect changes in models.

pgadmin.tagline: The community's official graphical client for PostgreSQL.
pgadmin.description: Free PostgreSQL administration tool, with a SQL editor, object browser, execution plans and monitoring.

tableplus.tagline: Native database client, fast and with a clean look.
tableplus.description: Native graphical client for several relational databases and Redis, with spreadsheet-style data editing, filters and tabs.

metabase.tagline: Open source BI: questions and dashboards without writing SQL.
metabase.description: Business intelligence tool where anyone explores database data, creates charts and dashboards, with an optional SQL editor.

dbt.tagline: Data transformations in SQL with tests and documentation.
dbt.description: Tool that transforms data inside the warehouse itself using versioned SQL, with tests, documentation and dependencies between models.

valkey.tagline: Open source fork of Redis, maintained by the Linux Foundation.
valkey.description: In-memory data structure store compatible with Redis, created after Redis's license change and maintained by the community.

memcached.description: Distributed in-memory caching system, focused on simplicity and speed for plain keys and values.

couchdb.tagline: Document database with an HTTP API and multi-master sync.
couchdb.description: JSON document database accessible over HTTP, with replication between instances and offline-first sync support.

netlify.tagline: Hosting and deploy for sites and frontends, with previews.
netlify.description: Platform to publish static sites and frontends with a deploy on every push, PR previews, serverless functions and forms.

railway.tagline: Platform to publish apps and databases in a few clicks.
railway.description: PaaS that publishes applications, databases and services straight from the repository, with usage-based billing and a visual interface.

render.tagline: Simple PaaS for sites, APIs, databases and scheduled jobs.
render.description: Hosting platform with Git-based deploys for web services, workers, cron jobs and managed Postgres databases.

fly-io.tagline: Runs containers close to users, across multiple regions.
fly-io.description: Platform that runs applications in containers (microVMs) across dozens of regions, with its own CLI, volumes and private networking.

digitalocean.tagline: Simple cloud, with VPS, managed databases and Kubernetes.
digitalocean.description: Cloud provider focused on simplicity, with droplets (VPS), managed databases, Kubernetes, storage and predictable pricing.

google-cloud.tagline: Google's cloud, strong in data, AI and Kubernetes.
google-cloud.description: Cloud platform with compute, databases, data analytics (BigQuery), AI and Kubernetes (GKE), with a limited free tier.

azure.tagline: Microsoft's cloud, integrated with .NET, Windows and Microsoft 365.
azure.description: Cloud platform with a wide range of services, strong integration with the Microsoft ecosystem and hybrid options for enterprises.

nginx.tagline: High-performance web server and reverse proxy.
nginx.description: Light, very fast web server, reverse proxy and load balancer, present across much of the internet.

caddy.tagline: Web server with automatic HTTPS and simple configuration.
caddy.description: Go web server and reverse proxy that obtains and renews HTTPS certificates automatically, with a lean configuration file.

traefik.tagline: Reverse proxy that configures itself with Docker and Kubernetes.
traefik.description: Reverse proxy and load balancer that discovers services automatically in Docker, Kubernetes and other orchestrators, with automatic HTTPS.

helm.description: Packages Kubernetes applications into parameterizable charts, making it easy to install, upgrade and roll back versions in clusters.

argo-cd.description: Keeps the Kubernetes cluster state in sync with manifests in a Git repository, showing differences and allowing rollbacks.

ansible.description: Automation tool that configures servers and deploys applications with YAML playbooks, without installing agents on machines.

pulumi.tagline: Infrastructure as code in TypeScript, Python, Go and other languages.
pulumi.description: Describes cloud infrastructure using ordinary programming languages, with loops, functions and tests, instead of a dedicated declarative language.

opentofu.tagline: Open source fork of Terraform, maintained by the Linux Foundation.
opentofu.description: Infrastructure as code tool compatible with Terraform, created after the license change, with open governance.

prometheus.tagline: Collects and stores metrics, with alerts and the PromQL language.
prometheus.description: Monitoring system that scrapes metrics by pull, stores them as time series and allows queries and alerts with PromQL.

loki.tagline: Cheap log aggregation, inspired by Prometheus.
loki.description: Log system that indexes only labels instead of full text, which lowers cost and pairs with Grafana and Prometheus.

opentelemetry.tagline: Open standard for traces, metrics and logs, with no vendor lock-in.
opentelemetry.description: Set of APIs, SDKs and a collector to instrument applications and send traces, metrics and logs to any observability backend.

datadog.tagline: Complete observability platform, as a service.
datadog.description: Managed service that brings together metrics, logs, traces, user monitoring and security in one platform.

podman.description: Container engine compatible with Docker's CLI that runs without a central daemon and allows containers without root privileges.

docker-compose.tagline: Defines and starts several containers from a YAML file.
docker-compose.description: Tool that describes an application with several services (app, database, cache) in a YAML file and starts everything with one command.

k3s.tagline: Lightweight Kubernetes in a single binary, for edge and small servers.
k3s.description: Certified Kubernetes distribution packaged as a small binary, ideal for edge, IoT, labs and modest servers.

vault.description: Stores and controls access to secrets (passwords, keys, certificates), generating dynamic credentials with auditing and rotation.

jenkins.tagline: Classic CI/CD server, self-hosted and plugin-extensible.
jenkins.description: Open source automation server with thousands of plugins to build, test and deploy, running on your own infrastructure.

circleci.tagline: Cloud CI/CD, fast, with advanced caching and parallelism.
circleci.description: Continuous integration and delivery service with YAML pipelines, caching, parallelism and runners on several systems.

turborepo.tagline: Fast monorepo builds, with local and remote caching.
turborepo.description: Build system for JavaScript and TypeScript monorepos that runs tasks in parallel and reuses results through caching.

nx.tagline: Monorepo platform with a dependency graph, caching and generators.
nx.description: Build system for monorepos with dependency analysis, affected execution, distributed caching, code generators and plugins.

k9s.tagline: Terminal UI to browse and manage Kubernetes clusters.
k9s.description: TUI that shows pods, logs, events and cluster resources in real time, with shortcuts to inspect, edit and restart.

coolify.tagline: Self-hosted PaaS: your own Vercel/Heroku on your server.
coolify.description: Open source platform to publish apps, databases and services on your own servers with Git deploys, HTTPS and a web dashboard.

tailscale.tagline: Mesh VPN based on WireGuard, with no configuration.
tailscale.description: Private network that connects your devices and servers securely, with login-based identity and no open ports.

testing-library.tagline: Tests components the way users use them, not by internal details.
testing-library.description: Family of libraries that query the interface by accessible roles and text, encouraging tests that reflect real usage.

mocha.tagline: Flexible test framework for Node.js and browsers.
mocha.description: Test framework that lets you choose the assertion and mocking libraries, with configurable output.

selenium.tagline: Veteran browser automation, in several languages.
selenium.description: Set of tools to automate browsers, supporting Java, Python, C#, JavaScript and others, with a huge ecosystem.

puppeteer.tagline: Controls Chrome from code: screenshots, PDFs and automation.
puppeteer.description: Node library that controls Chrome and Firefox over a protocol, used for automation, PDF generation and screenshots.

k6.tagline: Load testing written in JavaScript, with a Go binary.
k6.description: Load and performance testing tool where scenarios are JavaScript scripts, with detailed metrics and Grafana integration.

pytest.tagline: Python's de facto standard test framework.
pytest.description: Test framework with simple syntax (plain asserts), powerful fixtures and a large plugin ecosystem.

junit.tagline: The standard test framework for Java and the JVM.
junit.description: Unit testing framework for Java and Kotlin, with annotations, parameterized tests and extensions, the basis of almost the entire JVM stack.

msw.tagline: Mocks APIs by intercepting real network requests.
msw.description: Library that intercepts requests at the network level (browser and Node) to simulate APIs in tests and development, without changing application code.

faker.tagline: Generates realistic fake data: names, addresses, text and more.
faker.description: Library that generates fictitious data in dozens of languages, useful for tests, prototypes and seeding development databases.

stylelint.tagline: Modern linter for CSS, SCSS and the like.
stylelint.description: Linter that finds errors and enforces conventions in CSS, SCSS and other syntaxes, with over a hundred rules and plugins.

oxlint.tagline: JavaScript and TypeScript linter tens of times faster than ESLint.
oxlint.description: Rust linter from the Oxc project, with hundreds of ESLint-compatible rules and much higher speed.

ruff.tagline: Extremely fast Python linter and formatter, in Rust.
ruff.description: Single tool that replaces Flake8, isort, Black and others, written in Rust and much faster than the alternatives.

mypy.description: Checks Python type annotations without running the code, pointing out errors before execution.

pyright.tagline: Fast type checker for Python, from Microsoft.
pyright.description: Static type checker for Python, fast and strict, which is the basis of Pylance in VS Code.

golangci-lint.tagline: Runs dozens of Go linters in parallel, with caching.
golangci-lint.description: Linter aggregator for Go that runs dozens of checks in parallel, with caching and a single configuration.

shellcheck.tagline: Finds bugs and pitfalls in shell scripts.
shellcheck.description: Static analyzer for sh/bash scripts that points out common errors, quoting problems and unexpected behaviors.

hadolint.tagline: Dockerfile linter that enforces best practices.
hadolint.description: Analyzes Dockerfiles for bad practices and problems, and validates embedded shell commands with ShellCheck.

semgrep.tagline: Static security analysis with rules that look like the code.
semgrep.description: Static analysis tool that looks for vulnerabilities and patterns with rules written almost like the code itself, in dozens of languages.

snyk.tagline: Detects vulnerabilities in dependencies, code and containers.
snyk.description: Developer security platform that analyzes dependencies, code, containers and infrastructure as code, with suggested fixes.

trivy.tagline: Vulnerability scanner for containers, dependencies and IaC.
trivy.description: Simple, fast scanner that looks for vulnerabilities, insecure configurations and secrets in images, repositories and manifests.

codecov.tagline: Test coverage reports on pull requests.
codecov.description: Service that receives test coverage from CI and shows it in PR comments and dashboards, pointing out what was left untested.

knip.tagline: Finds unused files, exports and dependencies.
knip.description: Analyzes JavaScript and TypeScript projects to point out files, exports and dependencies nobody uses, helping clean dead code.

lighthouse.tagline: Audits a page's performance, accessibility, SEO and best practices.
lighthouse.description: Google tool, integrated into Chrome, that measures performance, accessibility, SEO and best practices and suggests improvements.

axe-core.description: Library that finds accessibility problems in pages, integrated with Playwright, Cypress, Jest and browser extensions.

locust.tagline: Load testing in Python, with scenarios written in code.
locust.description: Load testing tool where user behavior is described in Python, with a web interface and distributed execution.

testcontainers.tagline: Starts real databases and services in disposable containers during tests.
testcontainers.description: Libraries that start Docker containers (databases, queues, etc.) during integration tests and discard them at the end.

stryker.tagline: Mutation testing: measures whether your tests actually catch bugs.
stryker.description: Introduces small changes to the code and checks whether tests fail, revealing weak tests that pass even with broken code.

dprint.tagline: Fast code formatter, extensible through WebAssembly plugins.
dprint.description: Rust formatter with plugins for several languages, configurable and much faster than Prettier.

chromatic.tagline: Visual testing and UI review from Storybook.
chromatic.description: Service from Storybook's makers that captures component images on each commit and highlights visual differences for review.

aider.tagline: AI pair programming in the terminal, integrated with Git.
aider.description: Command-line tool that edits your repository's code by chatting with AI models, committing the changes in Git.

cline.tagline: Open source coding agent inside VS Code.
cline.description: VS Code extension that acts as an agent: reads the project, edits files and runs commands with your approval, using the model you choose.

continue.tagline: Open source coding assistant for VS Code and JetBrains.
continue.description: Open source extension that brings AI chat, autocomplete and editing to the editor, with local or cloud models of your choice.

codex-cli.tagline: OpenAI's coding agent for the terminal.
codex-cli.description: OpenAI's open source programming agent that runs in the terminal, reads and edits project files and runs commands in a sandbox.

gemini-cli.tagline: Google's coding agent in the terminal, powered by Gemini.
gemini-cli.description: Google's open source command-line agent that uses Gemini models to understand the project, edit files and run commands.

ollama.tagline: Runs language models on your machine with one command.
ollama.description: Tool that downloads and runs open language models locally, with a compatible API and a simple CLI.

lm-studio.tagline: Graphical app to download and chat with local models.
lm-studio.description: Desktop app to discover, download and run open language models locally, with chat and a compatible API server.

llama-cpp.tagline: LLM inference in C/C++, efficient even on ordinary CPUs.
llama-cpp.description: C/C++ inference engine for language models, with quantization and support for CPU, GPU and Apple Silicon; the base of several local tools.

vercel-ai-sdk.tagline: TypeScript toolkit for AI apps, with streaming and multiple providers.
vercel-ai-sdk.description: Vercel library for building chats, agents and structured text generation with a single API across several model providers.

langchain.tagline: Framework to chain LLMs, tools and data.
langchain.description: Python and JavaScript framework for building LLM applications: chains, agents, tools, memory and integrations with vector databases.

llamaindex.tagline: Framework to connect LLMs to your data (RAG).
llamaindex.description: Framework focused on ingesting, indexing and querying your own data for use with LLMs, with connectors for dozens of sources.

hugging-face.tagline: AI model and dataset hub, and the Transformers library.
hugging-face.description: Platform with hundreds of thousands of open models, datasets and demos, plus the Transformers and Datasets libraries to use them.

mcp.tagline: Open protocol to connect AI agents to tools and data.
mcp.description: Open standard for exposing tools, data and prompts to AI applications through servers, with SDKs in several languages.

n8n.description: Automation platform with a visual flow editor and hundreds of integrations, which can be self-hosted or used in the cloud; source-available license (fair-code).

v0.tagline: Generates React interfaces from descriptions, by Vercel.
v0.description: Vercel AI tool that generates React and Tailwind components and pages from text or images, with preview and code.

chatgpt.tagline: OpenAI's AI assistant, for chatting, coding and analyzing.
chatgpt.description: OpenAI conversational assistant to write, code, analyze data and files and research, with free and paid plans.

claude.tagline: Anthropic's AI assistant, strong in code and long texts.
claude.description: Anthropic conversational assistant for coding, writing and analyzing long documents, with free and paid plans.

notion.tagline: Documents, wikis and databases in a single workspace.
notion.description: Collaborative workspace that combines documents, wikis, tasks and databases, with an API and a large template library.

linear.tagline: Fast issue and project management, made for product teams.
linear.description: Task and project management tool with a very fast interface, cycles, roadmaps and GitHub integration.

excalidraw.tagline: Virtual whiteboard with a hand-drawn look.
excalidraw.description: Browser diagram and sketch editor with a hand-drawn look, real-time collaboration and image export.

mermaid.tagline: Diagrams from text, right in Markdown.
mermaid.description: Generates flowcharts, sequence diagrams, ER and others from plain text, with native support in GitHub, GitLab and many editors.

bitwarden.tagline: Open source password manager, in the cloud or self-hosted.
bitwarden.description: Password manager with browser, desktop and mobile clients, end-to-end encryption and the option to host the server.

homebrew.tagline: Package manager for macOS and Linux.
homebrew.description: Package manager that installs command-line tools and apps on macOS and Linux with a single command.

fzf.tagline: Interactive fuzzy finder for any list in the terminal.
fzf.description: Interactive command-line filter that searches approximately across files, history, branches and any list of text.

ripgrep.tagline: Extremely fast file search that respects .gitignore.
ripgrep.description: Regular expression search tool for directories, much faster than grep, which by default skips files in .gitignore.

jq.description: Tool to filter, transform and format JSON in the terminal, with a compact query language.

bat.tagline: A cat clone with syntax highlighting, numbering and Git integration.
bat.description: Cat replacement that shows files with syntax highlighting, line numbers, automatic paging and Git change markers.

httpie.tagline: Terminal HTTP client with friendly syntax and colored output.
httpie.description: Command-line client for APIs, with intuitive syntax, JSON by default, syntax highlighting and sessions.

bruno.tagline: Open source API client that keeps collections as files, in Git.
bruno.description: API client for REST and GraphQL that stores collections as text files in your repository, with no required account or cloud.

neovide.tagline: Graphical interface for Neovim, with animations and GPU rendering.
neovide.description: Graphical client for Neovim written in Rust, with GPU rendering, cursor animations and smooth scrolling, keeping all your configuration.
